# Responsible data use — student workbook

Unit 2 Week 12: two privacy/ethical-testing lessons and two project evaluation/demonstration lessons. Draft for teacher review.

1. Distinguish privacy, security, ethics and law using one desk decision.
2. Explain personal versus sensitive information; why an ID/date combination may identify a borrower; synthetic data versus relabelled real data.
3. Analyse R01–R08 in responsible-data-scenarios.csv. Record benefit/purpose, affected people, evidence, relevant course principle, justified action and a limitation. Do not claim every school has identical legal obligations.
4. Explain APP 3, 6, 10 and 11 in your own words using a desk example. Refer to the official text for exceptions. Explain why consent, encryption and deleting names each have limits.
5. Explain the federal/WA distinction in the chapter's dated legal-context note. Name the source and date; identify when operational advice would be needed.
6. Review responsible-data-scope.md. Decide which actions are in/out of scope and why; the document itself does not grant testing authority.
7. Explain the purpose of ethical hacking and penetration testing, required authorisation and handling of an unexpected out-of-scope finding.
8. Complete responsible-data-review.csv: field purposes, access, disclosure, retention, actual evidence, implemented/tested/proposed status and improvement.
9. Demonstrate project reports, targeted changes, invalid-input checks and a separate restored copy. Evaluate every acceptance criterion as met/partly met/not met, citing evidence.
10. Review and explain the database, SQL, ER/dictionary, tests, privacy/security decisions and evaluation. Use synthetic public examples; follow the teacher’s approved storage/retention process.

No live-system testing or personal-data collection is needed for this activity. Recheck the legal-context note before reuse; classroom reasoning is not an operational permission grant.
